svg.title: Diagram of what USPS pages say about a Return Receipt. What it shows: the recipient's signature, the date of delivery and the actual delivery address if different. Bought at the time of mailing; it cannot be bought after mailing. Green card, PS Form 3811: mailed to the sender after delivery; the form is attached at mailing and the mail is endorsed Return Receipt Requested; the card cannot be viewed online; Priority Mail Express is marked Form 3811 only. Electronic: bought at a Post Office, then requested on the USPS Tracking website with an email address; if requested before delivery, usually available within 48 hours of delivery, and if the item is already delivered and the record complete, processed right away; kept two years. If it did not arrive: ask for the delivery record within 90 days of purchase with PS Form 3811-A; the fee is refunded only if USPS fails to provide the signature, unless the item was refused, unclaimed or returned to the sender. The pages differ on how the email address is given and on the refund timing.
svg.text: USPS Return Receipt
What the USPS pages say
1. What it shows
The recipient's signature, the date of
delivery and the actual delivery address
if it differs. Bought at the time of
mailing; it cannot be bought after.
2. Green card (PS Form 3811)
Attached at mailing; the mail is endorsed
"Return Receipt Requested." Mailed to the
sender after delivery. Cannot be viewed
online. The Related Tracking Number
tracks the card, not the mailpiece.
Priority Mail Express: marked Form 3811 only.
3. Electronic
Bought at a Post Office, not on USPS.com.
Requested on USPS Tracking with the
article number and an email address.
Requested before delivery: usually
available within 48 hours of delivery.
Already delivered and recorded: processed
right away. Kept two years. Courts decide
its legal status.
4. If it did not arrive
Ask for the delivery record within 90
days of purchase: PS Form 3811-A at a
Post Office, with your receipt. The fee
is refunded only if USPS fails to provide
the signature, unless the item was refused,
unclaimed or returned to the sender.
Where the pages differ
Email choice: the Basics FAQ, the DMM and
the Electronic FAQ describe it
differently. Refund timing: two wordings
that the pages do not reconcile.
Sources: USPS FAQs 000006076, 000007257;
DMM 503 section 6.0; read Nov. 24, 2026
